analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING 1) Payrolls Preview, 2) Equities Update, 3) BoE Recap and 4) New Gold Forecasts
key_insights: GS US Economics (Ronnie Walker) forecasts October nonfarm payrolls of +75k, above consensus of +65k and last month's +29k.

GS leans toward a stronger payrolls reading for two reasons. Alternative job-growth measures it tracks averaged about 70k in October. Job growth tends to rebound in October after a slow September that follows a late Labor Day, by an average of about 50k from the September pace.
GS forecasts the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.2% on a rounded basis, in line with consensus, and sees risks skewed toward a lower reading.

Richard Chambers (Co-Head of US IRP) says duration markets have been well supported since the Fed last Wednesday. He notes a modest 0.03% decline in the unemployment rate would print 4.1%, and calls that very doable given September jobless claims.
Chambers argues a 4.1% print could reprice the front end higher and keep the Fed on path for a December hike and more, given risk-off sentiment, a more patient Fed and lower oil.

Arvind Giridhar (Global Head of Volex Trading) says option-market event weights for NFP have been lower for much of this year, reflecting the labour market's diminished weight in moving Fed policy expectations. He says the Fed is more sensitive to inflation than to the labour market, at least in the direction of data beats.

Giridhar says the recent rates rally was partly driven by left-tail concerns about growth and the health of the AI trade. Upper left vol has been bid into the rally, wing receivers have been in demand on the front end, and skew has reshaped to the receiver side, raising the risk premium for rate cuts. He says no labour market weakness supports this so far.

Giridhar sees the asymmetry in payrolls reaction as larger for a miss than a beat. He expects a solid number now but more labour market weakness over the next several months as enterprises need to see a return on growing AI spend, and says the front end remains a buy on dips.
The Equities Update, BoE Recap and New Gold Forecasts sections named in the title are not present in the supplied text.
